name_en: Hasu gyoden — grilled Lake Biwa hasu fish glazed with sweet miso
summary_ja: 琵琶湖にすむ肉食性の淡水魚ハスを塩と酒でしめ、玉味噌を塗って焼く料理。網にかかると弱ってしまい流通しにくいため、限られた地域でのみ味わわれてきた琵琶湖八珍のひとつとされる。
summary_en: Hasu, a rare carnivorous freshwater fish native to Lake Biwa, is salted and grilled, then brushed with a sweetened miso glaze. Because the fish weakens quickly once netted and rarely reaches wider markets, this member of the "eight Lake Biwa delicacies" has stayed a local specialty.

name_en: Yaki moroko no dorozu — grilled honmoroko dipped in miso vinegar
summary_ja: 琵琶湖固有種ホンモロコを串に刺して焼き、味噌・砂糖・辛子・酢を合わせた「どろ酢」につけて食べる料理。冬から春の子持ちの時期が特に美味とされ、絶滅危惧種ながら養殖で今も食されていると伝わる。
summary_en: Honmoroko, a minnow found only in Lake Biwa, is grilled on skewers and dipped in "doro-zu," a muddy-colored sauce of miso, sugar, mustard, and vinegar. The roe-bearing fish of winter and spring are considered best, and though endangered in the wild, farmed stock keeps the dish on tables today.
source_title: 焼きもろこのどろ酢 滋賀県
